messages:
Olivia: Hey team — we hit a production issue where streaming responses from the /v1/streams endpoint are missing the final chunk about ~1-2% of the time. Client receives partial JSON and throws on parse. Request-id: req-5fa3b. Repro steps below.

Olivia: repro (simplified):
```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-large-v1","stream":true,"input":"Summarize..."}'
```
Output ends like: `... \"delta\":{\"content\":\"...\"}}]}\n` and then connection drops. No final `finish_reason` or trailing `}\n` — client gets `Unexpected end of JSON input`.

Ana: Sorry you're running into this — can you paste the raw chunked output (with curl -v) and confirm whether this is hosted or Dedicated? Also which SDK/version is the client using? Any proxy between client and Redwood?

Olivia: Hosted. No enterprise proxy on our side. Using node-fetch 3.2.0 in a server that proxies responses to our web clients. I captured verbose curl output:

```
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (18.205.93.12) port 443 (#0)
> POST /v1/streams HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.ai
> Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
> Content-Type: application/json
> Transfer-Encoding: chunked
>
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< content-type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
< transfer-encoding: chunked
< x-request-id: req-5fa3b
<
data: {"id":"resp-abc","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"Summary line 1.\n"}}]}
data: {"id":"resp-abc","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"Summary line 2.`

* Connection #0 to host api.redwood.ai left intact
```

Olivia: Immediately after that curl exits and our node-fetch handler throws `SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input` when we try to parse the accumulated stream.

Sam: Thanks, that output is helpful. We saw a similar pattern in the last week — nginx ingress proxies (version 1.12.3) can close backend connections when an upstream SSE stream has a short idle window before final flush, which effectively truncates the last chunk. The symptoms (chunked TE, SSE content-type, x-request-id present, then connection close with incomplete json) match INC-1428.

Sam: Quick checks for you:
- Do you have a reverse proxy between your node process and Redwood?
- Can you try `curl -v --no-buffer` and see if the stream stays open a bit longer?

Liam: Adding to Sam — there's also an unrelated bug in runtime 1.4.2 where `finish_reason` can be omitted on the last event when a connection drops mid-flush. We fixed it in runtime 1.4.3, but ingress upstreams can still cause the chunk to be cut off. Two mitigations: send server-side keepalive/ping SSE comments every ~700ms, or enable the SDK resume feature which uses `Last-Event-ID` to attempt resumed delivery.

Ana: For immediate mitigation on our side, can you try proxying through a connection that preserves chunked transfer and doesn't time out early? If you're using nginx we recommend `proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Connection ''; proxy_read_timeout 90s;` — that helps prevent the proxy from aggregating and then closing before the final flush.

Ana: Also as a client-side workaround, buffer until `end`/`close` event fires and only attempt JSON parse then, rather than parsing on every chunk boundary. Example Node pattern: 
```js
const res = await fetch(url, opts);
let buf = '';
res.body.on('data', (chunk) => { buf += chunk.toString(); });
res.body.on('end', () => {
  try { const parsed = JSON.parse(buf); /* handle */ } catch (e) { /* fallback */ }
});
```
Olivia: I added a short keepalive ping (SSE comment `:\n\n`) from our edge for testing and retried 10 times — streaming completed successfully 9/10; seems much better. We can hold that as a temporary. Can you advise ETA for a permanent fix?

Sam: Good news — ingress 1.12.4 with a fix for premature connection close is scheduled for a phased deploy next week (rolling across regions). Runtime 1.4.3 containing the finish_reason fix is also in the release queue — final QA tomorrow. I'll link your support case to INC-1428 and request priority validation for hosted customers who reported this.

Sam: Work items:
- Short term: Recommend keepalive pings on customer edge or set `proxy_read_timeout`/`proxy_buffering off` if you manage a proxy.
- Mid term: SDK resume support (`sse_reconnect: true`) will be documented and encouraged.
- Long term: ingress + runtime fixes (1.12.4 + 1.4.3) to stop truncation and ensure `finish_reason` is always emitted.

Olivia: Thanks — can you add me to the validation loop? I can provide logs from my failed runs. Also, is there a formal workaround to detect truncation server-side (so we don't surface parse errors to end users)?

Liam: We can add a short-lived token in the final event payload (e.g. `{"_end":"<sig>"}`) that SDKs can assert; we will also add a server-side checksum header on responses as a detection mechanism — planning that for the 1.4.3 release. For now, detect truncation by: if connection closed and last event does not include `finish_reason` or expected trailing sentinel, treat as incomplete and attempt client-side retry with `Last-Event-ID`.

deploy-bot: Created support ticket TKT-2026-987 and linked to internal incident INC-1428.

Ana: I'll follow up in TKT-2026-987 and keep you updated as we roll the ingress patch. Thanks for the detailed repro, Olivia — that made triage fast. :thumbsup:
